brief: Three faults, one subject: the town names more than it admits to naming, less than it draws, and some things it has deliberately hidden. (a) `cv.style.cursor = live ? 'pointer' : 'default'` keys on `answersTouch(x,y)`, which is the SOWABLE-cell test — so everything #113 opened up (roof birds, windows via `FACES`/`faceAt`, the vanes, the tree crowns) is findable on a desktop only by accident, and the naming and the affordance disagree. The cursor should become a hand wherever the town has a name to give. (b) The roof furniture is not named at all: `drawWashLine`, `drawWaterTank`, `drawPigeonLoft` and `LOFTS[]` put 24 pieces on the near roof — at a phone size the most pointable objects in the frame — and they say nothing, while `livingAt`, `pavingAt` and `FACES` answer for everything else in the town. Give them lines the way #113 gave the birds theirs: off what they ARE, in the town's own words, never a second table of boxes. (c) `nearHidden(y, sy)` is draw-side only — it is called inside `drawBird`/`drawCat`, not in the hit test — so a walker or bird behind the sill is still hit-tested and still named. Make the hit test read the same predicate the renderer does.
successLooksLike: At 390x844 and 1600x950, a real `mousemove`/tap driven onto a water tank, a pigeon loft, a line of washing, a window and a vane turns the cursor to a hand and returns a line; a point behind the sill returns nothing and shows no hand. Quote it as a table against HEAD, the way #113 did.
avoid: No new `OFFERS[]` entry — the queue is full and this is the affordance for tools already advertised. No new `R()` draw: this should hash-match HEAD at pinned instants, which is the whole proof that it is an interaction change and not a draw change. And do not prove it with `lookAt(project(...))` — that skips the event, which is exactly where #113 found a 16 px screen-space bug.
